questions.text: Which statement best defines spirometry?

answers.text: The measurement of arterial pH, PaCO2, and PaO2
The measurement of air entering and leaving the lungs
The measurement of oxygen saturation during sleep
The direct visualization of the airways

questions.text: In the PAINT and CBABE memory aids, PAINT is associated with which type of problem?
Which set belongs with the CBABE flow/obstruction memory aid?

answers.text: Cystic fibrosis, bronchitis, asthma, bronchiectasis, emphysema

answers.text: They do not require a mouthpiece

questions.text: Predicted reference values for spirometry are compared according to which patient factors?

answers.text: Weight, blood pressure, pulse, and temperature
Smoking status, oxygen device, diagnosis, and medication list
Occupation, sputum color, cough frequency, and sleep quality

questions.text: A PFT value is considered normal when it is:

answers.text: Greater than or equal to the LLN

questions.text: How are pack years calculated?

answers.text: Years smoked divided by packs per day
Packs per day x years smoked
Years since quitting x packs per week

questions.text: During the FVC maneuver, what should the patient do after inhaling maximally to TLC?

answers.text: Take several normal tidal breaths only
Forcefully exhale until completely empty at RV
Remove the nose clips and cough

questions.text: How many acceptable and reproducible efforts should be obtained during spirometry?
A sub-maximal blast is identified by low peaks on the flow-volume curve. What is the expected test implication?
Excessive extrapolated volume usually indicates which start-of-test problem?

answers.text: Extra breath at the end of the test
Leak after the test is complete

questions.text: For a patient with FVC less than 2 L, extrapolated volume must be less than:
Which middle-of-test issue makes an effort unacceptable when it exceeds the listed threshold?

answers.text: A normal tidal breath before the maneuver
FIVC - FVC greater than 0.100 L or 5% of FVC, whichever is greater

questions.text: What is FVC?

answers.text: The volume expired as forcefully as possible after maximum inhalation
The average flow rate during the middle half of FVC
The maximum flow rate attained during FVC
The ratio of FEVt to FVC

questions.text: In obstructive disease, why can FVC be less than SVC?

answers.text: A higher lower limit of normal

questions.text: Which FEV1 percent predicted range is classified as severe in the lesson?
Which timed interval is the most commonly used FEVt value and best value for grading airway obstruction severity?
Which finding suggests obstructive disease according to the lesson's ratio table?
What does FEF25%-75% measure?

answers.text: Maximum flow rate at the very peak of the loop
Average flow rate during the middle half of an FVC maneuver
Total exhaled volume after maximum inhalation
The ratio of FEVt to FVC

questions.text: Which spirometry value is effort dependent and should be evaluated for reproducibility before diagnostic interpretation?
On a flow-volume loop, what do the X-axis and Y-axis represent?

answers.text: X-axis = time in seconds; Y-axis = volume in L
X-axis = flow in L/sec; Y-axis = time in seconds
X-axis = volume in L; Y-axis = flow in L/sec

questions.text: What change is considered significant airway reversibility after bronchodilator testing?

answers.text: FEV1 or FVC increase greater than 12% and 200 mL
Any PEFR increase, regardless of reproducibility
